nav.label: Navigation
home.p: Upload one frame, compare it with palettes from famous films, adjust lift, gamma, and gain, then export a LUT for CapCut, Premiere Pro, or DaVinci Resolve. Free, and your photo never leaves the browser.
home.h2: From one frame to a LUT file
step1.d: Pick one JPG or PNG frame from your Rec.709 footage. ColorGrad picks out its five dominant colors.
step2.d: Choose a look from a famous film. The reference palette becomes the starting position of the color wheels, with an explanation.
step3.d: Your grade becomes a 33-point .cube file, ready to load in the editor you already use.
footer: helps video editors understand color grading instead of just pasting presets. All processing runs in your browser. Film palettes are approximations of dominant colors, with no film images or clips. Assumption: footage is Rec.709 (not Log).
drop.text: Drag one frame here, or choose a file.
slider: Slide to compare before and after
calib: Colors on your screen depend on monitor calibration. Treat the result as a starting point, then check it again in your editor.
refs.title: Reference look
guide.capcut: LUT support depends on the CapCut version and has not been verified on every version. In recent versions, look for the LUT import option under Filter or Adjustment, then choose the .cube file.
guide.premiere: Open the Lumetri Color panel, then Creative. In the Look menu choose Browse, and pick the .cube file.
guide.davinci: Copy the .cube file into DaVinci's LUT folder, then on the Color page right-click a node and choose LUT, or Refresh LUT if it does not show up.
note.neutral: {k} is left neutral because the reference {tone} are nearly gray.
note.shift: {k} pushes the {tone} toward {color}, following the {tone} of the {film} palette.
feat1.d: The five main colors of your frame, computed in Lab color space.
feat2.d: Eight references from famous films as a starting point for grading.
feat3.d: Lift, gamma, and gain with a real-time WebGL preview.
feat4.d: Everything runs in your browser. Your photo is never uploaded.
holo.h2: A LUT ready for your editor
holo.d: One .cube file holds your whole grade. Load it in CapCut, Premiere Pro, or DaVinci Resolve.
